output.answer_markdown:
In its fiscal 2022 10-K, IFF said operating cash flow is the primary source of funds for capital investment needs, dividends paid to shareholders and debt service repayments. It anticipated that cash flows from operations and availability under existing credit facilities would be sufficient to meet investing and financing needs, and believed existing cash balances were sufficient for debt service [2].

On the N&B transaction, the N&B Term Loan Facility was funded on February 1, 2021 as a $1.250 billion senior unsecured term loan, split into a $625 million three-year tranche (2024 Term Loan Facility) and a $625 million five-year tranche (2026 Term Loan Facility) [2]. After the Merger, IFF assumed N&B's debt financings, including both term loan facilities and Senior Notes totaling $6.250 billion with maturities of 2 to 30 years [2]. N&B's pre-Merger debt was used to fund the Special Cash Payment to DuPont and related transaction fees and expenses [2].
